name: Eliab
overview: Eliab, a male from the tribe of Reuben, is identified in Numbers 16:1 as the father of Dathan and Abiram. This Eliab should not be confused with another Eliab from the tribe of Zebulun mentioned in Numbers 1:9. His role is primarily defined by his family connections within the tribe of Reuben.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliab means 'G-d is my father,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name. This proper name is recorded in Numbers 16:1 and is not indicated to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Eliab is the father of Dathan and Abiram, as stated explicitly in Numbers 16:1. He is also connected as a descendant of Reuben and is related to Nemuel and Pallu, indicating a notable family lineage within the tribe of Reuben.
scriptureSignificance: Eliab's significance in Scripture centers on his position as the father of Dathan and Abiram, who are key figures within the tribe of Reuben. The distinction that he is not the same Eliab mentioned from Zebulun highlights the importance of accurate identification in biblical genealogy. His lineage underscores God's providential arrangement of tribal families in Israel's history.
